prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1448; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received for a sideswipe that occurred while the insured was changing lanes. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the photos submitted with the first notice. They confirm several details of the reported impact, but there are no independent witnesses to the collision itself. The vehicle damage is consistent with the described impact, and no prior damage to the vehicle is known from the file or the carrier's records.

Entry 3: Confirmed the driver is named on the policy and that nothing in the file suggests the damage happened before coverage began. The claimant has described the seating position at the time of impact, but it is not yet fully clear where in the vehicle they were sitting, so I have requested a follow-up statement from counsel.

Entry 4: Medical records indicate a whiplash-type injury. The reported injury fits well with the kind and force of this crash, and no earlier injury to the same body area is known. Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.

Entry 5: The claimant's statement was taken through counsel. They added a few small details since the first account, but the core account of the lane change and contact has stayed the same across every telling.

Entry 6: Based on the photos, the vehicle damage, the medical course, and the consistent account, the file supports the claim as presented. Pending receipt of the follow-up seating statement, I am recommending the claim proceed to evaluation.
